name: Visual Color Discrimination
definition: The ability to match or detect differences between colors, including shades of color and brightness.

benchmark.name: Colors in Context
benchmark.model_or_system: Monroe et al. 2017 blended pragmatic listener ensemble (Le), which combines an RNN literal listener with a speaker-derived pragmatic listener
benchmark.metric: listener accuracy (%), test set, averaged over all conditions (far/split/close)
benchmark.human_reference: General adults with normal color vision (the task was built from Mechanical Turk human–human reference-game play)

benchmark.name: ColorBench
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on the Color Perception & Reasoning tasks combined (multiple-choice)
benchmark.human_reference: General adult workforce with normal color vision, i.e. people who match or discriminate colors in everyday work such as inspection, painting, retail or design support

benchmark.name: ColorBench
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on Color Perception & Reasoning tasks, overall
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population with normal color vision (the typical worker who matches or detects color differences on the job, e.g., in retail, production or design support).
